docs.title: Erosion brand kit
docs.text: The Erosion mark is a rounded phone cut into an E. Three rows of diagonal cuts step left as they descend. Fired-clay slats and split copper tips follow the phone’s right edge, and a single centered camera slot finishes the top.

docs.title: Download the artwork
docs.text:
Asset Use Primary logo · SVG · transparent PNG Light slides, articles, and print layouts Reverse logo · SVG · transparent PNG Dark slides and photography with a dark, quiet area One-color logo · SVG Single-ink printing and monochrome layouts Editable PowerPoint mark Ten individually editable vector shapes Standalone mark · SVG · 512 px PNG Icons, avatars, and small placements Social card · 1200 × 630 PNG · editable SVG Link previews, announcements, and presentation covers CSS color tokens Website and digital campaign styling

Use the full logo at 120 px wide or larger. Below that, use the standalone mark down to 16 px. Leave at least the height of one shelf of the E clear on every side. The logo SVGs contain paths so they scale and print without installing a font.

docs.title: Marketing materials
docs.text:
Set headlines in a bold sans serif such as Inter, with Georgia Italic for short emphasis. Use a monospace face for Rust and technical labels. Keep body copy in Basalt on Chalk. The reverse treatment uses Chalk text and Copper accents on Basalt.

The soil-layer backdrop uses the colored bands from the social card. On the homepage, the sample screenshots sit in front of those layers.

The Rust gear beside the headline is the unmodified logo from the Rust project’s artwork collection, used under CC BY 4.0.

docs.title: Using device capabilities from Rust
docs.text: Controls Gallery → Device utilities exercises clipboard, Keychain/Keystore, authentication and haptics with disposable sample data. Capability calls use the same route and revision bridge as native controls.

docs.title: Enable an app
docs.text:
Use a small .xcconfig under ios/config named for the capitalized Android Gradle module (for example, gallery → Gallery.xcconfig). The Gradle build reads the same simple NAME = value declarations as Xcode. Set the iOS target's Debug and Release config files to this file, apply the DeviceCapabilities XcodeGen template and expose MRustCapabilities and the applicable usage-description settings in the target Info properties, as in Gallery and Field Catch. These are packaging steps for a new application. A new Rust screen in an enabled app needs only Rust changes.

Setting Meaning MRUST_CAPABILITIES Space-separated entries from files photos camera share audio location maps secure biometrics clipboard haptic rtc tilt. An absent declaration enables none. MRUST_CAMERA_USAGE, MRUST_MIC_USAGE, MRUST_LOCATION_USAGE, MRUST_FACE_USAGE User-facing purpose strings. Use the Face ID string for protected secrets as well as standalone authentication. MRUST_MAP_STYLE Android style filename in the app assets or an HTTPS style URL. The demo loads worldwide vector tiles and labels from OpenFreeMap as the camera moves. Uncached regions need internet access. The bundled offline map covers central San Francisco with 4,827 active street segments from San Francisco Public Works. Street geometry is distributed under the Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License. DataSF source. Supply licensed tiles and attribution for a production basemap.

Gradle merges permissions for enabled capabilities and installs a private FileProvider for the camera and share sheet. Android uses MapLibre Native 11.8.0 only in map-enabled apps. iOS uses system MapKit. A map of saved pins works with location access denied. Device permission prompts occur when the user invokes the feature.

docs.title: Issue requests
docs.text:
Keep an increasing request ID in the app model. Push an Effect::Capability { id, request } into the app's effects queue and handle HostEvent::CapabilityResult { id, outcome } in update. Compare the ID with the operation you are expecting. Capture the ID before opening another screen. Cancel with Effect::CancelCapability { id }. Camera, picker, and share UI can move the app out of the foreground while an operation is pending.

Task Rust request or control Capture or choose a photo Operation::CapturePhoto, Operation::PickPhoto; display the returned asset with asset.image("Photo").key("preview"). Import, export, share Operation::ImportDocument, Operation::Export { asset }, Operation::Share { text, assets }. Android reports Presented when it opens the chooser. UIKit reports completion or cancellation when the sheet closes. Record a memo Operation::Record emits Recording. Issue StopRecording or DiscardRecording with its own ID. The original request receives the final asset or cancellation. Play a memo Operation::PlayAudio { asset }, PauseAudio, ResumeAudio, SeekAudio { millis }. The original play request receives progress with position and duration in milliseconds, then a terminal result. Cancel it to release the player. Get location Operation::Locate { watch: false } returns one Fix. With watch: true it emits fixes until canceled, backgrounded, or its owner leaves. Each includes coordinates, timestamp, accuracy in meters, and reduced-accuracy status. Display a map Control::Map { center, zoom: 13.0, recenter: 0, pins }.key("map"). Give it a height. Keep pin IDs and the control key stable; increment recenter for an explicit camera move. Handle HostEvent::Pick for a selected pin and HostEvent::MapIdle for the final viewport. Open directions Operation::Directions { point } opens the platform maps handler. Android tries a navigation intent, then a maps directions URL. Check access Operation::Permission { feature: Permission::Microphone }; Camera and Location are also supported. Operation::OpenSettings opens the app's OS settings. Android's external camera path checks hardware availability and uses a temporary URI grant. Store a small secret Operation::SecretSet { key, value, protected: true }, SecretGet { key }, SecretDelete { key }. Read returns Outcome::Text. A protected read requires the OS to authorize the key operation. Use protected: false for an ordinary app-private secret. Verify identity Gallery uses Operation::VerifyDeviceOwner for a system biometric or screen-lock prompt (screen lock on Android 9). A device without a secure screen lock reports SetupRequired. Operation::Authenticate requests biometrics specifically. Protected storage independently enforces read access. Clipboard and haptics ClipboardWrite { text }, ClipboardRead, Haptic { feedback: Feedback::Selection }. Trigger clipboard reads from an explicit paste action. Haptics also accept Success, Warning, and Firm. Gallery uses Firm for one stronger tap.

AssetRef contains a private identifier, display name and MIME type. Persist it alongside the note. Bytes remain in the app container. The file adapters stage writes, move completed files into place, and clean abandoned staging files on a fresh process. An in-process Android Activity recreation can resume a pending file picker. An interrupted capture after process death can be retried. Shares give the recipient temporary read access. The imported files and notebook are local to this app installation.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Use the commands in the repository’s sample guide (samples/README.md). Exercise clipboard and storage round trips in Controls Gallery. Check tactile feedback and device authentication on a physical phone.

docs.title: Create a standalone app
docs.text:
From the directory where you keep your projects, install the generator and create a repository for your app.

cargo install --git https://github.com/fwaris/erosion.git --rev 62683cae8cdf60c89a539e9389fa449eef63f271 --locked cargo-erosion
cargo erosion new hello-mobile --id com.example.hellomobile --name "Hello Mobile"
cd hello-mobile
cargo test --locked

With an Android device connected, run ./scripts/run-android.ps1 in PowerShell on Windows. With an iPhone simulator booted, run bash scripts/run-ios.sh on your Mac. Tap Increment and the count changes from 0 to 1.

Open src/lib.rs to change the counter. Add a variant to Msg, handle it in update, and bind a control to it in view. The generated AGENTS.md describes this pattern for contributors and coding agents. Share the repository with its lockfile. Teammates can use its local scripts directly. Screens and state

docs.title: Platform setup
docs.text: Android requires PowerShell 7, JDK 21, Android SDK Platform 35, Build Tools 36.0.0, NDK r27d, and the Rust targets aarch64-linux-android and x86_64-linux-android. On an Apple Silicon Mac install Xcode, an iOS simulator runtime, XcodeGen, and the Rust targets aarch64-apple-ios and aarch64-apple-ios-sim. Use rustup target add from the repository root.

docs.title: Run one sample
docs.text:
To explore the three framework examples, clone the Erosion repository and run these commands from its root. Each command builds, installs, and opens the selected application.

Sample Android on Windows (PowerShell 7) iOS on a Mac (Bash) Controls Gallery ./scripts/run-android.ps1 gallery bash scripts/run-ios.sh gallery Falling Blocks ./scripts/run-android.ps1 falling-blocks bash scripts/run-ios.sh falling-blocks Field Catch ./scripts/run-android.ps1 field-catch bash scripts/run-ios.sh field-catch

Android. Start an emulator or connect a phone with USB or wireless debugging enabled. With multiple devices connected, use adb devices -l and append -Serial <serial>.

iOS. Start an iPhone simulator, or pass its UDID to boot it, for example bash scripts/run-ios.sh gallery "$SIMULATOR_UDID". List simulators with xcrun simctl list devices available. For a paired physical iPhone, set DEVELOPMENT_TEAM to your Apple team ID and run bash scripts/run-ios.sh gallery --device "$IPHONE_UDID" with the phone unlocked. Find the device with xcrun devicectl list devices.

Field Catch multiplayer. Start cargo run --locked -p field-catch-broker in a separate terminal. Android forwards port 8787 automatically in local mode. An iOS simulator can use the broker on its Mac. For a physical iPhone or players on separate computers, follow the Field Catch network setup in the repository’s sample guide.

docs.title: Upgrade a generated app
docs.text:
1. In the app's Cargo.toml, set both Erosion Git dependencies to the same new commit. Run cargo update -p erosion-ui -p erosion-native-host and commit Cargo.lock. Preserve the Rust package name, Android application ID, iOS bundle ID, and app data keys so the installed app upgrades in place.
  2. Replace study.mobile.StudyActivity with dev.erosion.host.ErosionActivity in the Android manifest and in the component launched by scripts/run-android.ps1. Keep the existing rust.app metadata. For custom JNI callers, the bridge class is dev.erosion.host.ErosionBridge and its shared library is liberosion.so.
  3. In the XcodeGen project, change ios/Study.swift to ios/ErosionApp.swift and native-host/StudyBridge.h to native-host/ErosionBridge.h under the same framework checkout. Keep the existing RustApp value and scene declaration. Custom C callers now use erosion_exchange and erosion_release.
  4. Change Rust imports and matches from erosion_ui::Event to erosion_ui::HostEvent. Existing Application implementations and native factories continue to work. A single-screen counter can replace its adapter and export with erosion_ui::erosion_app!(Model::default, update, view); and remove the old adapter imports. Apps with lifecycle hooks can implement erosion_ui::app::DeclarativeApp and return an AppAdapter from their factory.
  5. Run cargo test --locked, then run the app's Android and iOS scripts. Install over the existing app and check a previously saved setting on both platforms.

docs.title: Push and pop a page
docs.text:
Keep Routes<Page> in the Rust app model. Start with Routes::new(Page::Library). Match the page returned by nav.current() to build its screen, and return nav.presentation() from the app’s presentation() method.

match event {
    HostEvent::Press { key } if key == "clip" => {
        self.nav.push(Page::Player(false), Transition::Fade);
    }
    HostEvent::Back => self.nav.pop(),
    _ => {}
}

Controls Gallery uses this pattern to open an exhibit. Use Transition::System for platform navigation, Fade for a crossfade, or Immediate for a synchronous page change. Return the route instance ID from Application::route. Late events from a previous route are discarded by the engine.

docs.title: Request a native operation
docs.text:
The app queues effects and drains them in effects(). Assign a fresh request ID for each operation and remember which request belongs to the current screen.

use erosion_ui::{capabilities::Operation, runtime::Effect};
let request = Effect::Capability { id: 42, request: Operation::PickPhoto };

On HostEvent::CapabilityResult, match the ID before applying the outcome. An Outcome::Asset contains a private asset reference that can be persisted with the note. Handle cancellations and permission denial explicitly. The device guide lists operations and sample setup.

docs.title: Deep links and local notifications
docs.text: An app can assign a stable note ID when saving and open links such as mrust-notes://note/2. Schedule a local notification with Effect::ScheduleReminder { id, title, url, delay_seconds }. Handle HostEvent::OpenUrl { url } in Rust so tapping the reminder routes to the same saved note as opening the link. Register the URL scheme when packaging a new app. Android may defer delivery when exact alarms are unavailable.

docs.title: Sample applications
docs.text:
Build and launch the samples from the workspace. Each sample has a Rust crate, an Android application ID, and an Xcode scheme.

docs.title: Controls Gallery
docs.text:
Layout Inputs & form state Keyed collections Motion & navigation Drawing surface Video surface Device utilities

Open Inputs to exercise native editing, switches, sliders, and date selection. Search by control name, such as slider, canvas, or clipboard. Layout demonstrates rows, columns, wrapping, overlays and adaptive panels. Device utilities gives clipboard, haptics, authentication and secure storage their own instructions and results.

docs.title: Falling Blocks
docs.text:
Start the game, move or rotate the piece, and drop it. The Rust model owns timing, board state, and collision detection. The drawing surface receives the updated board. Pause and return to the game to exercise lifecycle behavior.

Model, message, and update explains how the buttons and swipes reach the same game rules.

docs.title: Field Catch
docs.text: Create or join a Field to play with a partner. Field Catch uses typed UI messages and WebRTC callbacks, and returns native effects from its reducer. Model, message, and update

docs.title: Run regression checks
docs.text:
cargo test --workspace --release --locked -- --test-threads=1

On a dedicated Android test installation run ./scripts/test-samples-android.ps1 -Serial <serial>. On the Mac run bash scripts/test-samples-ios.sh "$SIMULATOR_UDID". The native tests create sample data. Physical camera capture, microphone quality, biometric success, and haptic feedback still need phone sign-off.

docs.title: Screens and state
docs.text: A generated app supplies a model, an update function, and a view. Erosion turns the view into native controls and delivers their bound messages to the app. For direct control of rendering and event dispatch, an app can implement runtime::Application.

docs.title: Model, message, and update
docs.text:
Use this optional pattern when several controls or events can change the same state. The model holds the current state. A message (Msg) names an intent. Update applies that intent to the model, and the view describes the screen from the resulting state.

use erosion_ui::{declarative::{button, strata_screen, text, ViewScreen}, design::Role, view};

#[derive(Default)]
struct Model {
    count: u32,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
enum Msg {
    Increment,
}

fn update(model: &Model, msg: Msg) -> Model {
    match msg {
        Msg::Increment => Model { count: model.count.saturating_add(1) },
    }
}

fn counter(model: &Model) -> ViewScreen<Msg> {
    view! {
        strata_screen(0, "Counter") {
            text("count", model.count.to_string(), Role::Body);
            button("add", "Add one").on_press(Msg::Increment);
        }
    }
}

erosion_ui::erosion_app!(Model::default, update, counter);

The single-screen adapter uses route zero and keeps one set of mounted bindings per app instance. To handle lifecycle, Back, or device replies, implement app::DeclarativeApp with your own message type. Its update receives bound messages and its on_host_event receives unbound HostEvent values. Return Box::new(AppAdapter::new(app)) from the native factory. Override the route and presentation hooks when your model owns a navigation stack.

docs.title: How the games use it
docs.text:
• Falling Blocks binds the Left button to Msg::Move(Move::Left). A left swipe is classified as Move::Left and reaches the same Game::apply_move rule. The game owns its board, score, and phase. The application adapter handles clock ticks, navigation, and saving the high score. Start with samples/falling-blocks/src/view.rs and follow the binding into src/lib.rs.
  • Field Catch binds both keyboard submission and the Join Field button to Msg::JoinField. Its reducer takes an AppInput, which can carry a UI message, a typed WebRTC callback, or another platform event. It returns the next model and effects for the host to execute, such as requesting GPS. Start with samples/field-catch/src/view.rs and follow AppInput and update in src/lib.rs. Navigation and effects

docs.title: Compose the view
docs.text:
A child block accepts immutable let bindings, if let, if/else, match with braced arms, and for. End leaf and component expressions with a semicolon. Return a ViewNode<Msg> for one control or a Fragment<Msg> for several siblings. A fragment adds no native container. Use item-derived keys in loops and give every interactive source a unique key across the whole screen, including toolbar and accessibility actions.

Use a toolbar { ... } block on the screen root. For example, a call action can be declared as toolbar_item("video-call", "Video call", "video_camera").enabled(can_call).on_press(Msg::VideoCall);. Toolbar conditions follow the same rules as body conditions. Import widgets::ViewModifiers for style methods such as .rounded(12). An existing keyed Node can be inserted directly. Wrap it with from_node to attach a typed native event binding. The complete example lives in samples/field-catch/src/view.rs.

docs.title: Build a keyed editor
docs.text:
use erosion_ui::{
    widgets::{button, column, field, ViewModifiers},
    Node,
};

fn editor(title: &str) -> Node {
    column("editor", vec![
        field("title", "Note title", title),
        button("save", "Save note").rounded(12),
    ])
}

Place editor(&self.title) in the children passed to widgets::screen. Give each sibling a unique, stable key. A key describes a control’s identity across renders. Changing it can replace the native field and interrupt an edit.

docs.title: Handle native input
docs.text:
In an existing app model with a title: String field and a save() method, the update branches for the editor look like this:

match event {
    HostEvent::Input { key, value } if key == "title" => self.title = value,
    HostEvent::Press { key } if key == "save" => self.save(),
    _ => {}
}

For a Control::List, give every Item its own persistent numeric ID. Handle HostEvent::Pick { key, id } using that ID, so filtering or reordering rows still opens the correct item.

docs.title: Choose an authoring style
docs.text:
Widget functions and chainable modifiers cover common controls. Use Control variants directly for more specialized declarations. The optional ui! macro constructs the same keyed nodes:

use erosion_ui::{ui, widgets::button};
let form = ui!("form" => Column [
    ui!("volume" => Slider { label: "Volume".into(), value: 35 }),
    button("save", "Save"),
]);

The engine compares successive screen descriptions and sends changes over a revisioned bridge. The declarative API, individual widget constructors and both macros use that update path.

docs.title: Register a separate app
docs.text: Add a crate under samples/, list it in the workspace, and depend on erosion-ui by path. Implement Application and export its factory with erosion_native_host::export_app!. Add the corresponding Android module in android/mobile/build.gradle and a dedicated XcodeGen project under ios/ (for example, ios/Gallery.yml). Use the same app selector for both hosts. After this initial setup, ordinary screens can be added entirely within the Rust crate.

docs.title: Strata starter style
docs.text:
Use strata_screen for Chalk and Basalt. All five sample apps use this builder. Tap the half-filled circle (the Theme button) in the navigation header to select System, Chalk, or Basalt. System follows the device appearance. Each sample remembers its own choice across launches.

use erosion_ui::widgets::{button, field, strata_screen};

let page = strata_screen(1, "Field note", vec![
    field("title", "Note title", ""),
    button("save", "Save note"),
]);

Chalk pairs a warm paper background with oxide actions. Basalt pairs charcoal green with copper actions. Both use sage for enabled switches, 48-unit minimum button heights, 12-unit button corners, and 16-unit default card corners. Explicit corner radii take precedence. Select Change accent on the Controls Gallery home screen to try the alternate patina accent.

docs.title: Surfaces, corners, and shadows
docs.text:
Import ViewModifiers to style a keyed node. This example groups a native text field and button inside a padded, elevated surface.

use erosion_ui::{
    design::Elevation,
    widgets::{button, column, field, ViewModifiers},
};

let form = column("form", vec![
    field("title", "Title", ""),
    button("save", "Save").rounded(16),
]).surface().padding(16).rounded(20).elevation(Elevation::Medium);

Elevation maps to Android view elevation and UIKit layer shadows. Use Role::Title, Secondary, Accent, and Error to distinguish text by purpose. Pass a theme into the screen builder:

use erosion_ui::widgets::theme;
let palette = theme("#F7F0E4", "#75461E", "#251D19", "#FAC08C");

The arguments are light background, light accent, dark background, and dark accent.

docs.title: Scrolling, wrapping, and rotation
docs.text:
Use column or row for a stack, scroll for a vertically scrollable viewport, and flow to wrap children to available width. For example, flow("actions", 8, buttons) uses a gap of eight logical units between items and lines. A native list handles row reuse.

For structural changes, handle HostEvent::WindowResized { width } and store WidthClass::from_width(width). The wide class starts at 600 dp or points. Gallery’s Layout exhibit switches the same three panels from a column to a row. Its wrap example sets Style::flow_item_width to 88 logical units.

docs.title: Widget motion
docs.text:
Rust declares target values on a stable key. The host animates between targets using the device display clock. In a view! child block, for example:

text("card", "Current score", Role::Accent)
    .scale(if model.expanded { 1.1 } else { 1.0 })
    .rotation(if model.expanded { 3.0 } else { 0.0 })
    .motion(Motion { duration_ms: 180, easing: Easing::EaseOut })
    .feedback(model.score_event, Feedback::Pulse);

Import the motion types from erosion_ui::design and the ViewModifiers trait from erosion_ui::widgets. Translation uses logical units, rotation uses degrees, and scale is uniform about the center.

  • Property change. Set opacity, horizontal or vertical translation, scale, or rotation with a duration and easing. A new widget starts at its declared target.
  • Conditional content. Attach .presence(Presence { enter: Some(PresenceEffect::FadeSlide), exit: Some(PresenceEffect::Fade) }) to the conditional child. Each side can be omitted. Removal immediately drops its input bindings. Eligible visuals finish a 180 ms exit.
  • Layout change. Attach .animate_layout(Motion { duration_ms: 180, easing: Easing::EaseOut }) to a row, column, or flow. Give each child a stable key so it can move and retain focus across reordering. Native scrolling lists handle row movement separately.
  • One-shot feedback. Change the event ID to replay a 240 ms pulse or shake on an existing widget. Keep the ID stable across unrelated renders. Update the score or validation result when the event arrives, independently of animation completion.

Controls Gallery’s Motion & navigation exhibit demonstrates all four. Reduced motion on iOS and disabled animators on Android apply the final state directly.

docs.title: Page transitions
docs.text: Use a navigation transition when an entire page changes. Navigation and effects describes system, fade, and immediate transitions.
